# docsbio-stickman-wasm

Wasm wrapper for smart-capture (idscan-engine-smart-capture)

## Local compilation

### Prequisites

A binary version of smart-capture-package is required -
smart-capture-package is the smart-capture binaries with
the required resource files added. Prebuild binaries for
this can be sourced from:

https://hunter.idscan.cloud/packages/smart-capture-package/wasm/

(develop is "vdev"). This should be downloaded and unpacked into:

    .pkgs/smart-capture-package

relative to this directory.

The build instructions require nvm and emsdk to be installed
as normal - installation instructions for those are out-of-scope.

The polly repo from https://github.com/idscan/polly needs to be
cloned to a local directory and environment variable POLLY_ROOT
needs to point to it.

## Extracting Prebuilt Binaries

To extract the prebuilt `smart-capture-package` binaries into the required directory, use the following command from the root of the repository:

```bash
mkdir -p .pkgs/smart-capture-package && tar -xzf .pkgs/smart-capture-package_wasm_vdev.tar.gz -C .pkgs/smart-capture-package
```

This will create the `.pkgs/smart-capture-package` directory if it does not already exist and extract the contents of the `smart-capture-package_wasm_vdev.tar.gz` file into it.

### Building the Module

To build the module, emcmake is used but is called from npm:

    npm install
    npm run build


### Testing

There is currently a smoke test that can be run via:

    npm test

#### Browserify tests

In order to run the smoke tests from a browser, some extra steps are needed.
- Install `browserify` and `brfs` node packages
- Execute the `browserify_smoke_test.sh` from within the build folder, for example with
    ```bash
    (cd _builds && bash ../browserify_smoke_test.sh)
    ```
- In the build folder, now you should have one `*-bundle.js` and `*.html` file per test.
Just open the `*.html` file in a browser, inspect the web page and look at the console.

#### Bigmagic-web functional tests

Bigmagic-web intragrates the `stickman.js` file in the final smart capture product.
We have included a test which somehow replicates this integration for debugging purposes.
To run it, please see the [instructions](test/bigmagic_web_test/README.md).

## Basic Use

See the smoke test source (test/smoke-test/smoke-test.js)
for hints on how to use the module. Note the way the module
is loaded:

    import stickmanModuleFactory from './stickman.js';
    const stickman = await stickmanModuleFactory()

This ES6 code replaces an earlier node-orientated scheme
that was based on require() but was not portable.

**Note:** here is an additional stickman.worker.js which
is assumed to related to javascript workers, but is not
seemingly documented anywhere.

## Identifying C++ Dependencies

Listing dependencies (for C++) is not automated, nor that simple to perform as
some interpretation is required, but can be done following the steps identified in this
section.

The dependencies can be grouped into three sections:
- That directly related to emscripted - the compiler and the libraries - so quote
the emscripten version itself.
- Anything directly referenced in the CMakeLists.txt itself, e.g. nlohmann-json.
- Modules pulled in from the upstream Engine module, libsmart-capture.a. This is
what takes the most interpretation to identify.

libsmart-capture.a is a "fattened" static library, in that all other modules that
the Engine "smart-capture" module itself depends on are added into that library.
It might be thought that this list shows all the dependencies, but actually it
is somewhat misleading as it is a superset of what is used - e.g. only a fraction
of OpenCV functionality is actually linked to, let alone used, by this module,
so the list of extras in libsmart-capture.a is much longer then actually used.

To help fine the true list of dependencies, the build scripts generate map file
"output.map". This indirectly contains information about which .o files are
pulled in. We can process this file with the following command:

    perl -ne 'm/libsmart- capture\.a\((.*)_wasm_/ && print "$1\n"' output.map | sort -u

Typical output for this would be:

    libconfiguration-sc
    libimage-processing-sc
    libjpeg
    liblibcvprotobuf
    liblibopenjp2
    libobject-detection-sc
    libopencv_core
    libopencv_dnn
    libopencv_imgcodecs
    libopencv_imgproc
    libpng
    libsmart-capture
    libspdlog
    libz

We can group these:
- libconfiguration-sc, libimage-processing-sc, libobject-detection and indeed libsmart-capture
itself all related to direct submodules of the Engine smart-capture module, and are thus
not considered third-party dependencies.
- libopencv* and additionally liblibcvprotobuf and liblibopenjp2 are all part of the OpenCV
module. The particular version of OpenCV used can be found looking at the
cmake/configs/default.cmake file under https://github.com/gbgplc-internal/idscan-engine-hunter.
  - Note that different versions have different config branches, so vdev will map to
develop and releases will map to tags of the form sc-1.2.3.
- Other libraries (here libjpeg, libpng, lpbspdlog and libz) are also to be found under
hunter (respectively JPEG, PNG, spdlog and ZLIB). Again the specific versions can be
found from cmake/configs/default.cmake under hunter.
